name: High-Bar Barbell Back Squat
description: The high-bar barbell back squat places the barbell on the upper trapezius, just below the base of the neck. This position encourages a more upright torso throughout the movement, placing greater demand on the quadriceps compared to the low-bar variation. It is the squat style used in Olympic weightlifting as it closely mimics the receiving position of the clean and snatch.

execution.starting_position: Stand inside a power rack with the bar resting on the upper traps, below the base of the neck. Feet shoulder-width apart, toes turned out 15-25 degrees. Grip slightly wider than shoulders.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the rack hooks at upper-chest height. Position bar across upper traps, unrack with a controlled step back.
steps: Step 1: Brace the core fully and take a deep breath before beginning the descent.
Step 2: Break at the knees and hips simultaneously, keeping the torso relatively upright.
Step 3: Descend with knees tracking over the toes until the hip crease passes below the knee.
Step 4: Drive through the full foot and extend both the hips and knees to return to standing.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale and brace before descent. Exhale at the top of each rep.
common_mistakes: Excessive forward lean (more typical of low-bar)
Heels rising due to limited ankle dorsiflexion
Knees collapsing inward at the bottom
Losing upper back tension under the bar
safety_considerations: Set safety bars appropriately in the power rack
Develop adequate ankle dorsiflexion and hip mobility
Consider heel elevation with plates if ankle mobility is limited
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full depth requires hip crease below the top of the knee. The more upright torso allows greater depth for many lifters.
